requirement:
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.

A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not read any implementation source.

**Successful tracked reads are included when verification finishes, whether code or a model tool requested them.**
- Direct code reads: `graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` finishes the context and asserts that `record.dependencies` holds the `Dependency::Node` observations.
- Direct code reads: `fn[later_lighter_agent_calls_preserve_the_contexts_existing_trace]` asserts that direct reads and agent reads of node contents all land in the finished record. It also asserts that a later lighter ask leaves the trace unchanged.
- Direct code reads: `fn[concurrent_single_node_validations_keep_separate_traces]` asserts the node and edge dependencies in each persisted record from `Validator::verify`.
- Model tool reads: `agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` has the model call `read_node` and `outgoing_edges`. It asserts the observations, then finishes and compares `record.dependencies` with the persisted observations.
- Model tool reads: `fn[cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input]` covers source-tool observations.

**Each observation holds the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.**
- `fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` asserts the identity and fingerprint `fp(original)` for an empty string and for a large multi-byte string. It also shows that the fingerprint and contents are unaffected when the graph later changes.
- `fn[graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change]` has the graph change during a paged tool read. It asserts that the fingerprint value equals the original, supplied contents and that the pages concatenate back to that original.
- `fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` checks the fingerprint value `"x".repeat(18_000)` for the tool read.

**A failed read returns an error and invents no observation.**
- `fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` reads the missing node 9 and asserts the error `"missing"` and empty dependencies.
- `fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` reads the missing node 2 and asserts an error, with the dependency list unchanged.
- `fn[node_preparation_tool_errors_allow_recovery_without_recording_undelivered_contents]` makes a tool read fail in preparation. It asserts that the error reaches the model with `is_error` set and that dependencies stay empty.

**Repeating an identical observation adds no information.** In `fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]`, node 1 is read several times with the same "before" contents through `read` and `read_snapshot`. The graph read log shows the extra reads, yet the dependencies hold only one "before" entry.

**The same identity with two different fingerprints preserves both.** The same test changes node 1 to "after" and asserts the dependencies are `[Node(1, before), Node(1, after)]`. It also asserts the earlier saved snapshot is unchanged and that the finished record holds both entries.

The remaining tests bear on the requirement only indirectly. `fn[changing_one_criteria_input_does_not_invalidate_another]` covers how recorded inputs are used. I found no unmet obligation, so I report no gaps.
